info.title: WebMS Intra REST API
info.description: Internal portal platform REST API. Two mutually-exclusive auth modes are accepted on every endpoint: (1) an authenticated portal session (cookie-based) plus a valid CSRF token on write operations (passed via `X-CSRF-TOKEN` header or `csrf_token` body field), or (2) a site-scoped bearer API key (`Authorization: Bearer wbms_…`, minted at Admin → Integrations → API Keys). Bearer requests need NO CSRF token — CSRF protects cookie-based sessions from cross-site forgery and is meaningless for a bearer token that travels in an explicit Authorization header set by the calling code, never by a browser automatically. Bearer requests are tenant-pinned to the key's own site (regardless of the Host header) and are rate-limited per key (see `/api/v1/*` paths below). Every endpoint can be enabled/disabled per-site via the `api.{module}.{action}.enabled` setting; bearer requests resolve that flag against the KEY's site, not the host-detected default. An endpoint also follows its APP's own switch (Admin → Apps): when the app it belongs to is switched off for the organisation, every one of that app's endpoints, legacy and `/api/v1` alike, answers 403 with the message `The <app name> app is switched off for this organisation.`, before the per-endpoint setting is looked at. For a bearer request the app's switch is read for the KEY's site, whatever address the key is sent to. The `events` endpoints and the Event Team Hub endpoints belong to the Calendar app; the `users` endpoints belong to no app and are never refused this way. The `/api/v1/{resource}[/{id}]` paths are a thin RESTful facade: each verb maps onto the SAME handler file and the SAME `api.{app}.{action}.enabled` flag as its documented `/api/{app}/{action}` legacy alias — there are no separate permissions to manage. Events copied in from an outside calendar reach an API key exactly when a signed-out visitor could see them, in the same detail, unless the calendar — or a choice or rule covering the event — is set 'Don't show via API'.

sessionCookie.name: PHPSESSID
sessionCookie.description: Portal session cookie set on sign-in.

csrfToken.name: X-CSRF-TOKEN
csrfToken.description: CSRF token. Read from `<meta name="csrf-token">` in the portal HTML or from the session. Required on POST endpoints; ignored on read-only GETs.

bearerAuth.description: Site-scoped API key from Admin → Integrations → API Keys; scopes gate each resource:verb; rate-limited per key; CSRF-exempt.

Error.description: A refusal. `meta` was missing from this schema until 27 October 2026 even though every refusal carries it: ApiResponse::error() builds its envelope from the same meta() as ApiResponse::success(). That matters to a caller making several writes without reloading, because meta.csrfToken is where the replacement form token arrives - on a refusal as well as on a success.

status.description: Always the text "error" on a refusal.

message.description: What went wrong, in words meant for a person. Safe to show to the caller.

detail.description: Extra detail for diagnosis. Present ONLY when the installation has debug mode switched on, which is for administrators; on an ordinary installation this field is absent altogether, so a caller must not depend on it.

meta.description: The same envelope block a successful answer carries. Includes csrfToken when a session-authenticated write has just replaced the form token.

eventID.description: The event's own number, and the key `GET /api/events/detail?id=` takes. Assigned by the database; never sent by a caller.

eventName.description: The event's title as people see it. The one field never hidden from a caller whose details are limited.

eventSlug.description: The address-safe short name, so an event can be fetched by name instead of by number (`?slug=sunday-service`). Built by the portal from the title and unique within the organisation; a caller cannot choose it. **There is no collision handling:** two events given the same title in one organisation produce the same short name, and the second is refused by the database as a 500 rather than with a clear message.

description.description: The event's long text — an order of service, notes, what to bring. **Returned by `detail` only: `list` does not include it.** Emptied to null when `detailsLimited` is true.

startDateTime.description: **A reading on a clock, not a moment in history.** It is the time as written on the clock of the zone named in `timezone`; it is not UTC and carries no offset, so turning it into an instant means reading it in that zone. When the event starts. Returned as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` — a space, no `T`, no offset. (`format: date-time` was declared here until 30 October 2026 and was untrue: that means RFC 3339, which this is not.)

endDateTime.description: **A reading on a clock, not a moment in history.** It is the time as written on the clock of the zone named in `timezone`; it is not UTC and carries no offset, so turning it into an instant means reading it in that zone. When the event ends. Null when no end time was recorded. Returned as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` — a space, no `T`, no offset. (`format: date-time` was declared here until 30 October 2026 and was untrue: that means RFC 3339, which this is not.)

timezone.description: The time zone the start and end are a clock reading in: a full IANA name. An event has exactly one; there is no second zone field.

isAllDay.description: 1 when the event runs the whole day, so the clock times should not be shown. Sent as the number 1 or 0, never `true` or `false`.

locationName.description: The place in words — "Main Hall", "Zoom". Free text with no link to the venue records. Emptied to null when `detailsLimited` is true.

status.description: The event's state. A draft is returned only to a caller who may manage events (an administrator session, or a key with events:write).

isPublic.description: 1 when a signed-out visitor could see this event. For your organisation's own events it is the event's own setting. For an event imported from an outside calendar it is worked out from who may see it, so it is always 1 in a reply to an API key.

isFeatured.description: 1 when the event is promoted — pinned to the top of a listing, or shown on a highlights panel.

categoryName.description: The name of the category the event is filed under ("Worship", "Youth"). Null when it has no category, or the category was deleted. Deliberately NOT hidden from a caller whose details are limited.

typeName.description: The name of the event type ("Sunday Service", a preaching-plan entry). Null when none is set or the type was deleted. Also not hidden from a limited caller.

locationAddress.description: The address as free text, exactly as somebody typed it — it may run to several lines and is not broken into parts. Emptied to null when `detailsLimited` is true.

locationWebURL.description: A web link for the place or the event — a venue page, or a joining link for an online meeting. **`detail` only.** Not checked for being a valid address. Emptied when `detailsLimited` is true.

locationPhone.description: A telephone number for the place or the organiser. **`detail` only.** Not checked for format. Emptied when `detailsLimited` is true.

locationEmail.description: An e-mail address for the place or the organiser. **`detail` only.** Not checked for format. Emptied when `detailsLimited` is true.

locationGeoLat.description: The latitude of the place in decimal degrees, positive north, to seven decimal places. Kept only as a pair with `locationGeoLng` — one without the other is never stored. **Comes back as a string**, such as `"52.2053000"`, because the column is a decimal. Emptied when `detailsLimited` is true.

locationGeoLng.description: The longitude in decimal degrees, positive east, to seven decimal places. The partner of `locationGeoLat`. Also comes back as a string. Emptied when `detailsLimited` is true.

location.description: Canonical cross-repo location object (#456) — additive; the legacy location* fields above are kept for backward compatibility.

imported.description: True when the event was copied in from an outside calendar (#514); false for the organisation's own events. The outside calendar itself, and every internal import or external setting, are never returned.

detailsLimited.description: True when this caller may see only the event's title, date and time (#514). Its description, every location field, the location object's contents, host and partner names, images and venue are then null. Only ever true for an imported event; the organisation's own events are always sent in full to a caller who may see them.

Event.description: **This shape is not everything `detail` returns.** That endpoint reads the event record directly and so also sends about thirty-five fields this shape does not declare — among them the series, host and partner organisations, the pictures, capacity and registration settings, submission and moderation state, the venue and room numbers, and the created and updated stamps. `list` conversely returns FEWER fields than this shape: it omits `description`, `locationWebURL`, `locationPhone` and `locationEmail`, which come only from `detail`.

Location.description: Canonical location object shared byte-for-byte with the ProjectBookIT/ProjectEPass location contract (#456). Every field may be null; consumers must tolerate a partial object.

name.description: The place's name in words, from the event's `locationName`. An empty value in the database comes back as null.

line1.description: The street or building line. **For an event this holds the WHOLE free-text address**, which may run to several lines — it is not a first line in the postal sense.

line2.description: A second address line — a flat, building or estate. **Always null when the place came from an event.** An event keeps only four location columns, and no event endpoint joins to the venue records, so this part of the shared shape is never filled by this API. The field exists because the shape is shared unchanged with ProjectBookIT and ProjectEPass, where venues do carry it.

city.description: The town or city. **Always null when the place came from an event.** An event keeps only four location columns, and no event endpoint joins to the venue records, so this part of the shared shape is never filled by this API. The field exists because the shape is shared unchanged with ProjectBookIT and ProjectEPass, where venues do carry it.

region.description: The county, state or region. **Always null when the place came from an event.** An event keeps only four location columns, and no event endpoint joins to the venue records, so this part of the shared shape is never filled by this API. The field exists because the shape is shared unchanged with ProjectBookIT and ProjectEPass, where venues do carry it.

postcode.description: The postcode or ZIP code. **Always null when the place came from an event.** An event keeps only four location columns, and no event endpoint joins to the venue records, so this part of the shared shape is never filled by this API. The field exists because the shape is shared unchanged with ProjectBookIT and ProjectEPass, where venues do carry it.

address.description: The address split into parts. Always present as an object, even when every member inside it is null. For an event only `line1` is ever filled.

latitude.description: The latitude in decimal degrees, positive north, to seven decimal places. The same value as `Event.locationGeoLat`, given here as a number rather than a string.

longitude.description: The longitude in decimal degrees, positive east, to seven decimal places. The same value as `Event.locationGeoLng`, given here as a number.

geocodedAt.description: When the latitude and longitude were last worked out by a look-up. **This one really is a moment in history, in UTC**, written RFC 3339 with a `Z` — unlike the event times, which are readings on a clock. **Always null when the place came from an event.** An event keeps only four location columns, and no event endpoint joins to the venue records, so this part of the shared shape is never filled by this API. The field exists because the shape is shared unchanged with ProjectBookIT and ProjectEPass, where venues do carry it.

geocodeSource.description: Which service produced the coordinates. Checked against the permitted list on the way IN but passed through unchanged on the way out, so a value stored before that check existed is returned as it stands. **Always null when the place came from an event.** An event keeps only four location columns, and no event endpoint joins to the venue records, so this part of the shared shape is never filled by this API. The field exists because the shape is shared unchanged with ProjectBookIT and ProjectEPass, where venues do carry it.

eventName.description: The event's title. Required. Blank or spaces only is refused with 400. **Not shortened and not length-checked by the portal**, so a value longer than the column allows fails in the database and comes back as a 500 rather than a clear refusal.

startDateTime.description: Required. When the event starts, **written on the clock of `timezone`** — or of the organisation's own zone when `timezone` is left out. Any date text PHP can read is accepted, not only ISO 8601, and it is stored to the second. A value carrying its own offset is read as a moment and stored as that clock's reading at that moment. Unreadable text is refused with 400.

endDateTime.description: When the event ends, on the same clock as the start. Leave it out, or send an empty value, for an event with no end time. It must read as a date AND be no earlier than `startDateTime`, or the request is refused with 400; equal start and end is accepted.

timezone.description: Optional. The time zone the start and end are a clock reading in: a full IANA name, spelled exactly. Left out, the event takes its organisation's own zone. A start or end given with an offset of its own is a moment, and is stored as this zone's clock reads at that moment. A name the portal does not know is refused with 422 and nothing is created.

isAllDay.description: Say the event runs the whole day, so clock times need not be shown. Note the asymmetry: sent as a true/false value, but returned by `Event.isAllDay` as the number 1 or 0.

locationName.description: The place in words. **Left out, it is stored as an empty string rather than null**, and the reply echoes that empty value. **Not shortened and not length-checked by the portal**, so a value longer than the column allows fails in the database and comes back as a 500 rather than a clear refusal.

locationWebURL.description: A web link for the place, or a joining link for an online meeting. Silently shortened to 500 characters rather than refused, and **not checked for being a valid address**.

locationPhone.description: A telephone number for the place or the organiser. Silently shortened to 50 characters rather than refused. Not checked for format.

locationEmail.description: An e-mail address for the place or the organiser. Silently shortened to 255 characters rather than refused, and **not checked for being a valid address**.

locationGeoLat.description: Validated as a pair with locationGeoLng — either both present and valid, or the pair is stored as null (#456).

locationGeoLng.description: The longitude in decimal degrees, positive east. The compulsory partner of `locationGeoLat`: neither is stored without the other, and **sending one alone drops the pair in silence rather than refusing it**.

locationW3W.description: Bare canonical what3words form (no leading ///). A non-empty value that fails this pattern is rejected with a 422 (#456).

categoryID.description: The number of the category to file the event under ("Worship", "Youth"). **Not checked against the organisation's categories**, so a number that does not exist fails on the database link and comes back as a 500 rather than a clear refusal. Send null or an empty value for no category.

typeID.description: The number of the event type ("Sunday Service", a preaching-plan entry). **Not checked**, with the same 500 consequence as `categoryID`. Send null or an empty value for no type.

status.description: What state to create the event in. **Read this before using it: the portal, the database and this description have disagreed, and the fault is recorded as #676.** The database stores `draft`, `published`, `cancelled` or `postponed`. The two writers allow `draft`, `published`, `cancelled` or `archived` instead, which has two consequences, both measured: **`archived` is allowed by the writer and then refused by the database, giving a 500**; and `postponed` — a real stored value this API returns in `Event.status` — **cannot be set here at all** (create silently stores `draft` instead, update refuses with 400). Until #676 is settled, send only `draft`, `published` or `cancelled`. Note too that create silently falls back to `draft` for an unrecognised value while update refuses it with 400.

isPublic.description: Whether a signed-out visitor may see the event on the public calendar. **Defaults to true when the field is absent.** Note the portal reads this loosely, so the text `"false"` counts as TRUE — send a real true/false value.

isFeatured.description: Promote the event — pin it to the top of a listing, or show it on a highlights panel.

description.description: The event's long text — an order of service, notes, what to bring. Left out, it is stored as an empty string rather than null. **Not shortened and not length-checked by the portal**, so a value longer than the column allows fails in the database and comes back as a 500 rather than a clear refusal.

NoticeboardPoster.description: Poster as returned by GET /api/noticeboard/list (DB columns already mapped to the field names the board component reads).

id.description: Client-facing id; the literal string "p" + posterID.

title.description: The poster's headline — the main line of text on the tile. Never empty: a poster saved with a blank title is skipped rather than stored.

kicker.description: Short eyebrow line shown above the title.

category.description: The free-text grouping word the board shows and can filter by. Free text, not a fixed list; defaults to `Other`.

schedule.description: Whether this poster is a single dated occasion or a weekly one — read `date` for `once`, `weekday` for `weekly`.

date.description: Set when schedule=once; empty string otherwise.

time.description: 24-hour HH:MM, or empty string if not set.

location.description: Where the thing happens, as free text for people to read. An empty value means none was set.

link.description: Official event page. The board opens this when the enlarged poster is tapped a second time.

mediaType.description: Text-only posters (no image/canva) are reported here as "image" with an empty image URL.

canva.description: Canva embed URL, for mediaType canva.

thumb.description: Optional board thumbnail override for Canva posters.

colorIndex.description: Index into the board's built-in accent-colour palette.

serif.description: true = editorial serif title font, false = bold sans-serif.

PosterInput.description: One poster in the `posters` array sent to POST /api/noticeboard/save. The client always sends the FULL desired board state — any existing poster whose id is missing from the array is soft-deleted.

id.description: Pass the existing "p<posterID>" to update that poster. Omit, or use a fresh client-generated id (e.g. "p<timestamp>"), to insert a new one — an id that doesn't belong to this site is treated as new rather than overwriting another site's poster.

title.description: Required — rows with an empty/whitespace-only title are silently skipped.

kicker.description: The short line printed above the poster's title — an "eyebrow" such as "This Sunday" or "Youth". Decoration only; nothing acts on it. Left out, it is stored as an empty value rather than null.

category.description: A free-text grouping word the board shows and can filter by, such as "Community". **Free text, not a fixed list** — nothing checks it against anything. Defaults to `Other`.

schedule.description: Whether this poster is one dated occasion (`once`, read with `date`) or something that happens every week (`weekly`, read with `weekday`). **Anything that is not exactly `weekly` quietly becomes `once`** rather than being refused.

time.description: The start time written on the clock as `HH:MM`, 24-hour. A reading on a clock with no zone attached; send hours and minutes only. **Not checked** — a value the database cannot read as a time gives a 500 rather than a clear refusal.

location.description: Where the thing on the poster happens, as free text for people to read. Not a venue reference and not linked to the venue records.

link.description: http(s):// absolute or a root-relative ("/…") path only — any other scheme (e.g. javascript:) is silently stripped to empty.

mediaType.description: Server-side derived value wins: forced to "canva" if canva is set, or "text" if neither canva nor image is set.

image.description: Media URL for image/video posters. data: URIs are rejected with 422 — upload via the media library and pass its URL instead.

canva.description: Canva embed/share URL. Must start with https://www.canva.com/ or it is discarded.

thumb.description: An optional smaller picture to show on the board in place of the poster itself — used for designs whose embed cannot be drawn as a tile. Only a full `http://`/`https://` address or one starting with `/` is kept; anything else is stored as empty.

colorIndex.description: Which accent colour the board paints this tile in — a position in the board's own palette, not a colour value. **Not range-checked**, so a number outside what the column holds gives a 500.

aspect.description: The shape of the poster tile as a ratio, such as `4/5`, `3/4` or `1/1`. Free text passed straight to the board's styling; the format is not checked.

serif.description: Which title font the poster uses: true for the editorial serif face, false for bold sans-serif. **Read loosely — any truthy value counts as true, so the text `"false"` would switch it ON.**

V1SuccessEnvelope.description: Standard success envelope returned by every /api/v1/* and legacy /api/{app}/{action} endpoint.

status.description: Always the text `ok`. A fixed marker that the call succeeded, not a value that varies; a failure arrives in the error envelope instead.

data.description: Endpoint-specific payload — see each operation's response schema.

timestamp.description: The moment the portal built this answer, always in UTC, written as ISO 8601 to the second with an explicit `+00:00` — never a `Z` and never fractions of a second. It is the time of the ANSWER, not of the thing being described.

version.description: The portal's own version number, so a caller can tell which release answered. It comes from the single source of truth in the portal's code, not from the database and not from this description.

csrfToken.description: Present ONLY on a write (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) that was authenticated by the caller's login session and passed its anti-forgery check. The portal issues a brand-new anti-forgery token every time it accepts one, so the token you just sent is now dead. Use this replacement on your next write, or you will be refused with "CSRF check failed". Requests authenticated with a bearer API key never receive this field, because they carry no session for a token to protect.

meta.description: Information about the answer itself rather than the thing asked for. Always carries `timestamp` and `version`, and additionally `csrfToken` on a write made with a sign-in session.

status.description: Always the text `error`. The HTTP status carries what kind of failure it was.

message.description: A short sentence a person can read. **It is not a machine-readable code and not from a fixed list** — each handler supplies its own wording, so do not match on it; decide behaviour from the HTTP status.

detail.description: Only present when the server is running in debug mode.

timestamp.description: The moment the portal built this answer, always in UTC, written as ISO 8601 to the second with an explicit `+00:00` — never a `Z` and never fractions of a second. It is the time of the ANSWER, not of the thing being described.

version.description: The portal's own version number, so a caller can tell which release answered. It comes from the single source of truth in the portal's code, not from the database and not from this description.

csrfToken.description: Present ONLY on a write (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) that was authenticated by the caller's login session and passed its anti-forgery check. The portal issues a brand-new anti-forgery token every time it accepts one, so the token you just sent is now dead. Use this replacement on your next write, or you will be refused with "CSRF check failed". Requests authenticated with a bearer API key never receive this field, because they carry no session for a token to protect.

meta.description: The same block a successful answer carries: `timestamp` and `version` always, and `csrfToken` when a session write had already replaced the token before the refusal was decided.

groupLabel.description: The name of the group being counted — an age band or category such as "Adults", "Children" or "Visitors". Free text chosen by whoever records the count, not a fixed list. **Going over the length shown is REFUSED with 400**, not shortened.

headcount.description: How many people were counted in that group. Zero is allowed; a missing or negative value is refused with 400.

sortOrder.description: What order the groups are listed in on screen, lowest first. **Left out, it defaults to the entry's position in the list you sent** — not to 0 for every entry.

serviceTypeID.description: FK tblAttendanceServiceTypes; must exist for the current site.

sessionDate.description: The date the service or gathering being counted took place, on the organisation's own calendar. A plain date — no time, no zone. Must be exactly `YYYY-MM-DD`: a value such as `2026-7-19` or `19/07/2026` is refused with 400.

eventID.description: FK tblEvents; must exist for the current site.

notes.description: A free-text remark about this one count — why the number was unusual, what else was on. For people to read; nothing acts on it. An empty or blank value is stored as null.

counts.description: The breakdown of the headcount by group — one entry per group. May be left out or empty, which records a session with no breakdown. **Anything that is not a list is ignored in silence**, while a list containing something that is not an object refuses the whole request with 400.

AttendanceUpdate.description: PATCH-style — only fields present are touched. When `counts` is present, ALL existing headcount rows for the session are replaced (delete + re-insert).

serviceTypeID.description: Which kind of service or gathering this count belongs to. Only acted on when the field is present. It must already exist for your own organisation, or the request is refused with 400.

eventID.description: The diary event this count belongs to, if any. **Send null to detach the count** and leave it standing alone. A number must be an event of your organisation, not deleted, and **not imported from an outside calendar**.

sessionDate.description: The date the service or gathering took place — a plain date on the organisation's own calendar. Must be exactly `YYYY-MM-DD` when present.

sessionTime.description: The start time written on the clock as `HH:MM`, 24-hour. **Send null, or an empty value, to clear it.** When a value is given it must be exactly `HH:MM`.

notes.description: A free-text remark about this count. Send null, or an empty value, to clear it — an empty value is stored as null rather than as empty text.

counts.description: The breakdown by group. **This REPLACES the lot:** when the field is present every existing breakdown row for the session is deleted and these are put in its place, so sending an empty list wipes the breakdown entirely. Leave the field out to keep what is stored. **A value that is not a list is ignored in silence** rather than refused, so a malformed request can look as though it succeeded while changing nothing.

DocumentCreate.description: Accepts EITHER multipart/form-data (file field `file`, session-UI parity) OR application/json with base64 `fileContent` (shown here — the bearer/device mode). The real MIME type is sniffed from the file bytes (finfo) and checked against a server-side allowlist — the client-declared type/extension is never trusted.

title.description: The name the document is listed and searched under — what a member sees, not the file's own name on disk. **Going over the length shown is REFUSED with 400**, not shortened.

description.description: A longer note about what the document is, shown beside the title in the list. An empty or blank value is stored as null.

categoryID.description: FK tblDocCategories; must exist for the current site.

eventID.description: Ties the document to one diary event, so it appears with that event as well as in the general library. It must be an event of your organisation, not deleted, and **not imported from an outside calendar**.

isPublished.description: Whether members can see the document yet. False keeps it uploaded but hidden. **Defaults to true when the field is absent.** Because this endpoint also accepts a posted form, a text value is read loosely: it is trimmed and lower-cased first, so `0`, `false`, `False`, `FALSE`, `no` and empty all mean false, and any other text means true. A real true/false value is taken as itself. A JSON number `0` is not text and does not take that route — it is read as false.

fileName.description: Original filename — cosmetic only; the stored filename + extension are server-generated from the sniffed MIME type.

fileContent.description: Base64-encoded file bytes. Capped by the `documents.api.maxUploadBytes` setting (default 10485760).

DocumentUpdate.description: Metadata only — v1 has no file-replacement endpoint (rotate via create + delete).

title.description: The name the document is listed under. Only touched when the field is present, and it may not be set blank. **Going over the length shown is REFUSED with 400**, not shortened.

description.description: The longer note about the document. Send null, or an empty value, to clear it.

categoryID.description: Which library category the document sits in. **Send null to take it out of every category.** A number must be a category of your own organisation.

eventID.description: The one diary event the document belongs to. **Send null to detach it.** A number must be an event of your organisation, not deleted and not imported.

isPublished.description: Whether members can see the document. **Stricter than on create:** here any truthy value means true, with no list of accepted texts.

itemName.description: What was bought, in a few words — this line's description on the claim. **Going over the length shown is REFUSED with 400**, not shortened.

description.description: A longer note about this one line, where the name is not enough. For a person to read. An empty or blank value is stored as null.

unitCost.description: The price of ONE of this thing, in whole currency units and hundredths — **12.50 means twelve pounds fifty, not twelve and a half pence**. Rounded to two decimal places by the portal. Note there is no currency field anywhere on a claim, so which currency it is in is not recorded. Must be a number and not negative; zero is allowed.

quantity.description: How many of the thing were bought. Multiplied by `unitCost` by the portal to give this line's total. **Must be at least 1 — zero is refused.**

purchaseDate.description: The date this particular thing was bought — the receipt's date, separate from the claim's own `claimDate`. `YYYY-MM-DD` when given.

supplier.description: Who it was bought from — the shop or company's name, as free text. **Going over the length shown is REFUSED with 400**, not shortened.

ExpenseCreate.description: `lineTotal` and the claim `totalAmount` are always computed server-side from `unitCost * quantity` — never accepted from the client. New claims always land in 'Pending' status; the approval/status-transition workflow is DEFERRED to Phase 3 (no `PUT /api/v1/expenses/{id}` exists in v1).

deptID.description: FK tblDepts; must exist for the current site and be active (#517). Departments and user groups, and their memberships, are managed at Admin -> Departments / Admin -> Groups and are not readable or writable through this API.

claimTitle.description: A short name for the whole claim, so a treasurer can tell it apart in a list — "Youth weekend supplies", say. **Going over the length shown is REFUSED with 400**, not shortened.

claimDate.description: The date the claim itself is made — the date on the claim form, **not** the date anything was bought; each item carries its own `purchaseDate`. Must be exactly `YYYY-MM-DD`. Not checked for being in the past.

userID.description: REQUIRED for bearer (API-key) submissions only — the owning user, who must belong to the key's own site. Ignored/ not required in session mode, where the owner is always the authenticated session user.

items.description: The lines of the claim, one entry per thing bought. **At least one is required** — an empty list is refused with 400. The claim's total is added up from these by the portal; nothing a caller sends can set it.

UserCreate.description: Passwords are NEVER accepted here — the new account gets a random, unusable password hash and must go through the existing forgot-password flow to set a real one. `isAdmin` (portal-wide) is honoured in session mode only — a bearer key can never mint a portal admin, even with `users:write`; use `isSiteAdmin` (site-scoped) instead. #456 Chunk B: a member's Directory home coordinates/what3words (`latitude`/`longitude`/`what3words`/`visibilityCoords`, migration 181) are never readable or writable via this API in any mode — a deliberate safest-floor stance, since a bearer/session API caller has no per-viewer visibility-tier context to apply the member's own `visibilityCoords` gate against. #516: role holdings (`tblUserRoles`) are likewise never readable or writable through this API in any mode — grant or remove a role from the members page or Admin -> Roles instead. #517: group and department memberships (`tblUserGroups`, `tblUserDepts`) are likewise never readable or writable through this API in any mode.

emailAddress.description: The person's e-mail address. It is both how they are contacted and their sign-in name. Stored in lower case. **It must be unique across the WHOLE installation, not just your organisation**, so a clash is refused with 409 — and the wording is deliberately vaguer for an address that is in use somewhere you cannot see. Checking addresses is limited to a few attempts an hour, after which you are refused with 429 and a `Retry-After`.

fullName.description: The person's name as it is shown throughout the portal. One field — there is no separate first and last name. **Going over the length shown is REFUSED with 400**, not shortened.

isActive.description: Whether the account may be used. False creates it suspended — present, but unable to sign in. **Defaults to true when the field is absent.**

isAdmin.description: Administrator rights across the whole portal (every organisation). Honoured only for a signed-in (session) request from a global administrator; a session request from anyone else that would change it is refused with 403. Ignored for API-key requests.

isSiteAdmin.description: Administrator rights for THIS ONE organisation — managing its members, settings and data. **This is the one administrator flag a bearer API key may set**; the portal-wide `isAdmin` is not. It is stored against the membership, not the account, so it says nothing about any other organisation.

UserUpdate.description: Editable: fullName, isActive, isAdmin (session mode only), isSiteAdmin. Email address and password are excluded from v1 (silently ignored if present). A session caller can never deactivate their OWN account via this endpoint. Directory location fields are likewise excluded — see the `UserCreate` schema note (#456 Chunk B). Changing fullName or isActive on an account that belongs to a global administrator, has administrator rights across the whole portal, or also belongs (or used to belong) to another organisation is refused with 403 unless the caller is a global administrator using a signed-in session. Changing isSiteAdmin on a global administrator or a portal-wide administrator is refused the same way. An API key never counts as a global administrator.

fullName.description: The person's displayed name. Only touched when the field is present. Changing it on a protected account — a global administrator, a portal-wide administrator, or somebody who belongs to another organisation — is refused with 403 unless you are a global administrator on a sign-in session. **Going over the length shown is REFUSED with 400**, not shortened.

isActive.description: Whether the account may be used; false suspends it. **You can never switch off your own account here** — that is refused with 400. The same protection as `fullName` otherwise applies.

isAdmin.description: Administrator rights across the whole portal (every organisation). Honoured only for a signed-in (session) request from a global administrator; from anyone else a request asking for it is refused with 403. Ignored for API-key requests.

isSiteAdmin.description: Administrator rights for this one organisation, stored against the membership. The write happens only when the value actually changes. Changing it on a global or portal-wide administrator is refused with 403, and **an API key never counts as a global administrator**.

Asset.description: An asset as the portal returns it. **Two things to know before relying on this shape.** `list` returns a SUBSET: it selects 20 columns and one of them is stripped before the reply, so **19 fields** arrive — everything about warranties, licences, insurance, writing-down, labels and parentage is absent from it and comes only from `detail`. Conversely `detail`, `create` and `update` read the record with no join, so they do NOT carry `categoryName` or `locationName`, and they DO carry four fields this schema does not declare: `features` and `ownershipTerms` (both free text), `valuationDate`, and `isDeleted`. `licenseKey` and the public page's token are the only two stored fields deliberately removed from every answer.

assetID.description: The asset's own permanent number on this installation, assigned by the database.

siteID.description: Which organisation on this installation owns the asset. Always set from the signed-in organisation, or from the API key's own organisation — never from anything a caller sends. Absent from `list`.

assetKind.description: Whether this is a tangible item (`physical`) or a software licence, subscription or domain (`digital`).

name.description: What the asset is called — the one thing every asset must have.

description.description: A free-text description of the asset.

categoryID.description: The category the asset is filed under, within the same organisation. Becomes null if that category is later deleted.

categoryName.description: The category's name, joined in for convenience. **Returned by `list` only.** `detail`, `create` and `update` read the asset row directly with no join, so this field is absent from them — the schema said "list/detail only" until 30 October 2026, which was wrong.

locationID.description: Where the asset is kept or deployed, within the same organisation. Becomes null if that location is later deleted.

locationName.description: The location's name, joined in for convenience. **Returned by `list` only.** `detail`, `create` and `update` read the asset row directly with no join, so this field is absent from them — the schema said "list/detail only" until 30 October 2026, which was wrong.

model.description: The maker's model name or number.

serialNumber.description: The maker's serial number. Searchable, but **not unique** — two assets may carry the same one.

assetTagCode.description: The code printed on the asset's own label — what somebody reads off the sticker and types into a search. Unique within the organisation, although any number of assets may have none.

conditionState.description: What physical state the asset is in.

status.description: Where the asset stands in its working life — in use, away for repair, lent out, borrowed in, in storage, retired, disposed of, lost or stolen.

purchaseDate.description: The date the asset was bought.

purchaseStore.description: Where it was bought — the shop or supplier's name.

purchaseCostPence.description: What the asset cost, **in pence (minor units)** — send 89999 for £899.99, never a pounds-and-pence string. The currency is whatever `currency` says.

currency.description: The ISO 4217 three-letter code every money field on this asset is stated in, such as `GBP`.

warrantyExpiry.description: The date the maker's or supplier's warranty runs out.

warrantyDetails.description: Free-text notes about what the warranty covers.

licenseSeats.description: For a digital asset, how many seats — users or devices — the licence covers. **Null means the licence is not counted in seats**, not that it has none.

renewalDate.description: When the subscription or licence next falls due.

accessUrl.description: The sign-in or administration address for a digital asset.

depreciationMethod.description: How the asset's book value is written down over time: not at all, evenly across its life, or by a fixed share of what is left each period.

usefulLifeMonths.description: How many months the asset is expected to last, used as the period over which it is written down.

salvageValuePence.description: What the asset is expected to be worth at the end of its useful life, **in pence (minor units)** — send 89999 for £899.99, never a pounds-and-pence string. The currency is whatever `currency` says. Writing-down never takes the value below this.

currentValuePence.description: The book value as at the last valuation run, in pence (minor units) — 89999 means £899.99. **Read-only: no API call sets it**, and `readOnly` is declared here, so do not send it. Only the portal's own valuation job writes it, and only for assets written down evenly or by a share of the remainder. **Null therefore means "never valued", not "worth nothing"**, and an asset the job cannot work out is left untouched rather than zeroed.

insurancePolicyNumber.description: The policy or reference number for the cover.

insuredValuePence.description: The sum the asset is insured for, **in pence (minor units)** — send 89999 for £899.99, never a pounds-and-pence string. The currency is whatever `currency` says.

insuranceRenewalDate.description: When the insurance next falls due. This is the date the portal's reminder job reads.

isConfidential.description: Marks the asset as one not to be shown openly. **The effect is wider than hiding it from the public page:** `list` returns a confidential asset only to a signed-in administrator or asset manager — never to an API key and never to an ordinary member — and `detail` also allows a responsible owner. Anybody else gets a plain 404, not a 403, so the reply does not reveal that the asset exists.

publicPageEnabled.description: Whether this asset's public "lost and found" page may be shown at its scan address. **Not sufficient on its own:** the page appears only when the installation-wide setting is on AND this is 1 AND `isConfidential` is 0.

labelSymbology.description: Which barcode is printed on the asset's label: `qr` (links to the public lost-and-found page), `code128` (the asset tag code), `ean13`, `ean8`, `upca`, `upce` or `itf14` (that asset's own identifier of the kind named), or `qr+code128` for both.

parentAssetID.description: The asset this one is part of — used for kits, bundles and components. Always another asset in the same organisation; an asset can never be its own parent.

createdByID.description: The member who created the record. **An empty value means that person has asked to be forgotten** — the record is kept and only the name is removed — or that the record was made with an API key, which is not a person.

createdAt.description: When the record was created. Returned as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` on the server's own clock, with no offset — **not RFC 3339**, despite what `format` said here until 30 October 2026.

updatedAt.description: When the record was last changed. Also the order `list` sorts by, newest first. Same `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` form, no offset.

AssetCreate.description: Unlike the HTML `save.php` form this mirrors, money fields here are PENCE INTEGERS (not pounds-decimal strings), and an invalid ENUM value (assetKind/conditionState/status/depreciationMethod/labelSymbology) 400s rather than silently defaulting — **`currency` is the exception and is NOT in that list: an unusable code is quietly replaced with `GBP`** — see `_apps/assets/api/_coerce.php`. `licenseKey` travels as PLAINTEXT in the request body only — it is encrypted at rest and NEVER echoed back by any response. On update (PUT/PATCH), only fields present in the JSON body are touched; everything else keeps its current value.

name.description: What the asset is called. **The only required field.** Blank, or longer than 255 characters, is refused with 400. On an update, sending it blank is refused; leaving it out keeps the stored name.

assetKind.description: Whether this is a tangible item or a software licence, subscription or domain. An unlisted value is refused with 400.

description.description: A free-text description. Note the cap is counted in characters while the column is measured in bytes, so a very long description in a non-Latin script can still be refused by the database.

categoryID.description: The category to file the asset under. It must already exist **in your own organisation**; an id that does not resolve is **quietly turned into null rather than refused**.

locationID.description: Where the asset is kept. Same rule as `categoryID`: it must exist in your own organisation, and an id that does not resolve is quietly turned into null.

manufacturer.description: Who made it. Silently shortened rather than refused if it is longer than 150 characters.

model.description: The maker's model name or number. Silently shortened rather than refused if it is longer than 150 characters.

serialNumber.description: The maker's serial number. Silently shortened rather than refused if it is longer than 150 characters. **Not checked for being unique.**

assetTagCode.description: The code printed on the asset's label. Silently shortened rather than refused if it is longer than 50 characters. It must be unique within your organisation: a clash refuses the whole request with 409.

conditionState.description: What physical state the asset is in. An unlisted value is refused with 400.

status.description: Where the asset stands in its working life. An unlisted value is refused with 400.

purchaseDate.description: The date the asset was bought, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Anything unreadable is refused with 400; an empty value clears it.

purchaseStore.description: Where it was bought. Silently shortened rather than refused if it is longer than 255 characters.

purchaseCostPence.description: What the asset cost, **in pence (minor units)** — send 89999 for £899.99, never a pounds-and-pence string. The currency is whatever `currency` says. **Unlike the form this endpoint mirrors, it takes pence directly.** A value that is not a number, or is negative, is refused with 400; a decimal is accepted and its fraction dropped.

currency.description: The ISO 4217 three-letter code the money fields are in; it is upper-cased for you. **An unusable value is silently replaced with `GBP` rather than refused** — this is the one field in this body that does not refuse a bad value, and the schema's own summary wrongly listed it among those that do until 30 October 2026.

warrantyExpiry.description: When the warranty runs out, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Unreadable is refused with 400.

warrantyDetails.description: Free-text notes about the warranty cover. Silently shortened rather than refused if it is longer than 500 characters.

licenseKey.description: The licence key or activation code for a digital asset. **Write-only: it is sent as plain text, stored encrypted, and never returned by any endpoint.** Leaving it out, or sending it blank, means "leave the stored key alone" on an update and "no key" on a create — **so a key can never be cleared through this API**. Note the stored form is longer than what you send, so a very long key can be refused by the database.

licenseSeats.description: How many seats the licence covers. Null means it is not counted in seats. **Not range-checked**, so a negative number is accepted.

renewalDate.description: When the subscription or licence next falls due, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Anything unreadable is refused with 400.

accessUrl.description: The sign-in or administration address for a digital asset. Silently shortened rather than refused if it is longer than 500 characters. It must begin `http://` or `https://`, or the request is refused with 400.

depreciationMethod.description: How the book value should be written down. Only `straight-line` and `reducing-balance` are picked up by the valuation job that fills `currentValuePence`; `none` leaves it alone for ever.

usefulLifeMonths.description: Expected life in months, used as the period to write the value down over. **Not range-checked.**

salvageValuePence.description: What the asset should be worth at the end of its life, **in pence (minor units)** — send 89999 for £899.99, never a pounds-and-pence string. The currency is whatever `currency` says. Not a number, or negative, is refused with 400.

insurerName.description: The insurance company's name. Silently shortened rather than refused if it is longer than 150 characters.

insurancePolicyNumber.description: The policy or reference number. Silently shortened rather than refused if it is longer than 100 characters.

insuredValuePence.description: The sum to insure the asset for, **in pence (minor units)** — send 89999 for £899.99, never a pounds-and-pence string. The currency is whatever `currency` says. Not a number, or negative, is refused with 400.

insuranceRenewalDate.description: When the insurance next falls due, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Anything unreadable is refused with 400.

isConfidential.description: Hide the asset from the public lost-and-found page, and from anybody who is not a signed-in administrator, an asset manager, or (on `detail`) a responsible owner. **Read loosely: any value the portal considers truthy counts as true, so the text `"false"` would switch it ON** — send a real true/false value.

publicPageEnabled.description: Allow this asset's public lost-and-found page to be shown. **Defaults to true.** Not sufficient on its own — the installation-wide setting must also be on and `isConfidential` must be false. Read loosely, as `isConfidential` is.

labelSymbology.description: Which barcode to print on the label. An unlisted value is refused with 400.

parentAssetID.description: The kit or bundle this asset is part of. It must be an existing, undeleted asset in your own organisation, and cannot be the asset itself; **anything else is quietly turned into null rather than refused**.

EventHubResource.description: One row from an event's Team Hub Resources list (GET /api/calendar/hub-resources) — a link or a free-text note, grouped into a free-text section label.

resourceID.description: The portal's own number for this one entry in the event's resources list. Use it to tell entries apart; it means nothing outside this installation.

section.description: Free-text grouping label, e.g. "Before the event" / "On the day".

resourceType.description: Whether this entry is a link to somewhere else (`link` — read `url`) or a note kept in the portal (`note` — read `body`).

title.description: The entry's own heading — the words shown for the link, or the note's title.

sortOrder.description: What order entries appear in within their section, lowest first. Several entries may share a number, and those fall back to the order they were created in.

EventHubVideo.description: One row from an event's Team Hub video grid (GET /api/calendar/hub-videos). NEVER includes signing keys, playback tokens, or any cfstream.* credential — videoRef is the public provider ID/UID a player embeds against.

videoID.description: The portal's own number for this video in the event's grid. Local to this installation — **it is not the video service's own identifier**, which is `videoRef`.

provider.description: Which video service the video lives on, which tells a player how to read `videoRef`.

videoRef.description: YouTube 11-char ID / Vimeo numeric ID / Cloudflare Stream 32-hex UID — the public reference a player embeds against, never a secret.

title.description: The name shown under the video in the grid. Chosen by whoever added it, not fetched from the video service.

requiresSignedUrl.description: cloudflare only — whether playback requires a signed URL. Policy metadata, not a token.

allowedOrigins.description: cloudflare only — comma-joined allowed embed origins.

uploadStatus.description: How the video got here and whether it is ready to watch. `external` means somebody pasted a reference and there is no upload to wait for; the others are the stages of an upload made through the portal.

sortOrder.description: What order videos appear in on the grid, lowest first. Ties fall back to the order they were added in.

messageID.description: The message's own number. Use the largest one you have seen as `sinceID` to fetch only what is new.

displayName.description: The name the sender gave, as tidied by the portal when the message was accepted.

body.description: The message itself, already shortened to the installation's maximum length when it was accepted.

createdAt.description: When the message was sent, as the database stores it. This is NOT formatted or converted to the reader's time zone by this endpoint.

WorshipDisplayState.description: Where a running service plan has got to. A flat object: this is NOT the portal's usual {status, data, meta} envelope.

currentItemID.description: The item being shown, or null when the plan has no saved position yet. **Blanking or blacking the screen does NOT null this** -- the item is kept so the operator can return to it, so `isBlank` and `isBlack` are the only reliable test for a blank screen. A client that treated null as "blank" would go on showing the slide the operator just blanked.

currentSlideIndex.description: Which slide of the current item is showing, counting from zero.

totalSlides.description: How many slides the current item has. Always 1 for anything that is not a song.

isBlank.description: True when the operator has blanked the screen, leaving the display's own background.

isBlack.description: True when the operator has blacked the screen out entirely.

slideTitle.description: The current slide's heading. Empty when there is no current item.

body.description: The current slide's text. Empty when there is no current item.

itemType.description: What kind of item is showing, for example a song or a reading. Empty when there is no current item.

allOf.description: The plan's new position, plus the replacement form token. Note the token is a TOP-LEVEL field here, not `meta.csrfToken`, because this handler does not use the portal's usual envelope. A console drawn once and used repeatedly must carry it into the next request.

csrfToken.description: The replacement form token. Send this with your next request; the one you just used is now dead.

Tour.description: A guided tour of part of the portal.

tourID.description: The tour's own number. Send it back to `POST /api/tours/complete` when the person finishes.

tourKey.description: A short name for the tour, for example `welcome`.

version.description: Which version of the portal this tour was written for.

title.description: The tour's name, as shown to the person.

steps.description: The tour's steps, in order, as stored when the tour was written. The portal checks only that this is a non-empty list.

HymnSearchResult.description: One hymn or song found by a search. The fields present depend on where it came from -- read `source` first.

source.description: `hymnal` is this organisation's own hymn book, `song` its song library, `remote` an outside catalogue.

songID.description: The song library's own number. Present for `song` results.

author.description: Who wrote it, where that is known.

ccliNumber.description: The song's CCLI number, used for usage reporting, where it is known.

hymnalCode.description: Which hymn book it is in.

hymnNumber.description: Its number in that hymn book. Present on `song` rows; a `hymnal` or `remote` row carries its own fields from the hymn book it came from, which this schema does not list.

FlatError.description: A refusal from one of the handlers that answers OUTSIDE the portal's usual {status, data, meta} envelope and sends no `ok` field with it. Test the HTTP status, not a field.

error.description: What went wrong. **Its style differs by endpoint, so do not show it blindly and do not match on it.** The livestream ping sends a short machine word (`method`, `json`, `token`, `event`); the push endpoints send a sentence meant for a person, such as "Please sign in to turn notifications on for this device." Decide behaviour from the HTTP status, not from this text.

get.summary: List published events for the current site
get.description: **Who sees which events (#514):** a signed-in session sees what the calendar would show that person — public events, members-only events of an organisation they are an active member of (or administer), and events imported from outside calendars by their own level. An API key sees the organisation's own published events as before, and an event imported from an outside calendar exactly when a signed-out visitor could see it, in the same detail — unless its calendar, or a choice or rule covering it, is set 'Don't show via API'. Details are limited where `detailsLimited` is true (only title, date and time are sent). An event the caller may not see is simply absent from the list and from the counts.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Which page of the result to fetch, counting from 1. **A number below 1, or one that is not a number, is quietly moved to 1 rather than refused.**

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many rows to return per page. **A number outside the permitted range is quietly brought inside it rather than refused**, so asking for 5,000 gives you the maximum and not an error. Read `pagination.totalPages` in the answer to know how many pages there are.

data.description: The page of events, with the paging figures nested beside them. **This operation used to point at a shared `PaginatedListResponse` shape that nothing actually returned** — flat paging and an array called `items`. That shape was removed on 30 October 2026; the real reply is below.

events.description: The events on this page. Each omits `description`, `locationWebURL`, `locationPhone` and `locationEmail`, which come only from `detail`.

pagination.description: The paging figures for this answer. **Note they are nested here, not flat beside the rows.**

page.description: Which page was served, counting from 1.

limit.description: How many rows a page holds.

totalItems.description: How many rows match in all, counted under the same visibility rule as the rows themselves.

totalPages.description: How many pages the whole result takes.

hasNext.description: Whether a page follows this one.

hasPrev.description: Whether a page comes before this one.

get.description:
Returns up to 100 approved messages for one event, oldest first. Only messages with status `approved` are ever returned, so anything waiting, hidden or flagged is invisible here.

**Who may read it.** The handler itself asks for no sign-in. What a caller may see is decided per event: a public event is readable by anybody, and an internal one only by a signed-in person who may see it AND whose request came from one of the portal's own pages. An event the caller may not see returns 200 with an empty list, exactly as a made-up event number does, so the answer never reveals that an event exists.

**Polling.** Pass the `lastID` you were last given as `sinceID` to fetch only what is new. The portal sets no interval and enforces none.

Refused with 403 while the `chat.enabled` setting is not `true`.

post.summary: Post a message to a livestream's chat
post.description:
Adds one message to an event's chat.

**No sign-in and no form token are asked for**, because the embedded player runs on other people's websites. Four other things stand in their place: chat must be switched on; the event must be one the caller may see; the `sessionToken` must already exist for this organisation and event, having been created by a livestream ping; and the FIRST message from a given token must pass the bot check when one is configured.

**Over-long text is shortened, not refused.** `body` is trimmed to the installation's maximum and only then refused if nothing is left.

**The message may not appear at once.** The reply's `status` says which happened: `approved` is live immediately, `pending` is waiting for a moderator, and `flagged` was caught by the profanity check -- which marks the message rather than refusing it.

A missing event, an event in another organisation and an event the caller may not see all answer 401 `Unknown session`, deliberately, so the reply is not an existence oracle.

get.description:
The current position of a running service plan, for a projector screen or an operator's console to poll.

**This endpoint does NOT use the portal's usual `{status, data, meta}` envelope.** It answers its own flat object, and sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` so a display on another machine can read it. It carries none of the portal's usual security headers.

**It needs no sign-in.** The 64-character display token in `t` is the whole of the authority, and it is tied to one active plan in one organisation -- a token from another organisation answers 404.

**Polling:** the display polls about twice a second and the operator's console about once every one and a half seconds. Nothing is rate limited, so be careful what you point at it.

`totalSlides` is 1 for anything that is not a song.

**This endpoint does NOT use the portal's usual `{status, data, meta}` envelope**, and the replacement form token comes back as a **top-level `csrfToken`**, not as `meta.csrfToken`. A console that is drawn once and then used repeatedly MUST carry that value forward into its next request: without it every control works exactly once.

**What it changes is shared.** Every projector and console watching the same plan sees the move on its next poll of `/api/worship/state`. Moving into a song also records one line of song-usage reporting.

**Which refusals carry the replacement token:** it is absent from the 405, the 401, and the 400 raised by a failed token check, because all three are decided before a new token is issued. get.summary: The guided tour to offer this person next
get.description:
Returns the one tour the signed-in person should be shown next, or `null` when there is nothing to show. A tour already completed is never returned.

The welcome tour comes first when it is switched on, then the newest other tour. A tour limited to particular roles is offered to somebody holding one of them **or to any administrator**, who is never filtered out by the role test.

**It answers 200 with `data: null` rather than an error when it cannot read the tours at all**, so a portal with the tours table missing simply offers no tour. The only refusal is 401.

post.summary: Record that this person finished a tour
post.description:
Marks one tour as completed for the signed-in person, so it is not offered again. Always for the caller's own account: a tour cannot be completed on somebody else's behalf.

**Safe to call twice** -- a repeat leaves the original completion time alone.

Returns a replacement form token in `meta.csrfToken`, which a page that calls this more than once must keep. The 401, 405 and 403 below are decided before the token is issued, so they do not carry it.

**The sign-in check runs before the method check**, so a GET from a caller who is not signed in answers 401 rather than 405.

post.summary: Tell the portal a viewer is still watching
post.description:
Opens or refreshes a viewer's watching session, and closes it when they leave. This is what creates the `sessionToken` that `POST /api/livechat/send` needs.

**This endpoint does NOT use the portal's usual `{status, data, meta}` envelope**; it answers a flat `{"ok":true}`. It sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on purpose, because the embedded player runs on other people's websites, and it carries none of the portal's usual security headers.

**No sign-in and no form token are asked for.** A ping naming no event is accepted from anybody. A ping naming an event must name one the caller may see -- for an internal event that means a signed-in person whose request came from one of the portal's own pages. An internal, draft, other-organisation or made-up event all answer 404 alike, so the reply does not say which.

**A `leaving` ping skips the event check entirely**, because it only closes the caller's own session row. Note it matches on the token alone and is not scoped to an organisation.

token.description: The older embed snippet's name for `sessionToken`. `sessionToken` wins when both are sent.

eventID.description: The event being watched. Omit, or send 0, for a ping that names no event.

leaving.description: Send exactly `true` (not `"true"`, not 1) to close this watching session. Anything else counts as false.

200.description: The ping was recorded. A flat object, not the usual envelope.

204.description: Answer to a cross-origin pre-flight (OPTIONS). No body.

400.description: A flat refusal of this handler's own making.

404.description: A flat refusal of this handler's own making.

get.summary: What is booked, day by day, across a date range
get.description:
Returns the bookings for one venue, or for every venue, across a range of dates. For any signed-in person who may view venues; an API key cannot reach this.

**These are calendar dates, not moments.** `from` and `to` are read as plain dates and no time zone is applied to them.

**No cost information is ever returned** by this endpoint.

**One refusal covers four different causes.** A caller who may not view venues, a malformed or backwards date range, a range longer than 400 days, and a venue that does not belong to this organisation ALL answer 400 with the same `invalid-range` message -- deliberately, so the reply cannot be used to discover which venues exist.

parameters.description: First date to report on, as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last date to report on, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Must not be before `from`, and the range must be 400 days or fewer.

parameters.name: venueID
parameters.description: Limit to one venue. Omit, or send 0, for every venue this organisation has.

days.description: One entry per date in the range, keyed by the date as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

items.description: One booking. Cost columns are never included.

data.description: The payload for this call. The fields below sit inside it, alongside the envelope's own `status` and `meta`.

401.description: Not signed in.

get.summary: Whether a venue and room are free for a proposed time
get.description:
Classifies a proposed start and end against what is already booked, for the event editor to warn on a clash before anything is saved. For any signed-in person; an API key cannot reach this.

**`start` and `end` are readings on a clock, not moments in history**, and are used together with `tz`. **`tz` defaults to `Europe/London` and is NOT the organisation's own time zone** -- send it explicitly for any organisation that is not in the United Kingdom, or the answer will be an hour or more out.

**This endpoint does not refuse much.** A caller without permission to view venues, and an unknown venue, both answer 200 reporting that there is no venue to check, so it cannot be used to discover which venues exist. An unknown **room** is different: it falls back to classifying the venue as a whole rather than reporting nothing. It also does NOT check that `end` is after `start`.

parameters.description: The proposed start, as a reading on a clock: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: The proposed end, in the same form. May be left empty, which means no end is being proposed. Not checked against `start`.

parameters.name: tz
parameters.description: The time zone `start` and `end` are readings in, as a zone name such as `Europe/London` or `America/New_York`. **Defaults to `Europe/London`, not to the organisation's own zone.**

parameters.name: venueID
parameters.description: The venue to check. When omitted the `venues.calendar_default_venue` setting is used, which an organisation may set for itself.

parameters.name: roomID
parameters.description: A room within the venue. Omit to check the venue as a whole.

post.summary: Create a member account
post.description:
The legacy address of `POST /api/v1/users`, reaching the same handler. **This address does work** -- the handler's own method gate names POST, and that gate is only relaxed, never tightened, when the request arrives through the v1 facade.

**A signed-in caller must be an administrator.** A bearer key is gated by the `users:write` scope alone -- nothing in the key path performs an administrator test -- plus the `api.users.create.enabled` switch, **which ships switched off**.

**No password is set.** The new account gets an unusable one, so the person must use the existing forgot-password flow to choose their own.

**`isAdmin` is only honoured for a signed-in global administrator** and is silently ignored for a bearer key.

post.summary: Change a member account
post.description:
The legacy address of `PUT`/`PATCH /api/v1/users/{id}`, reaching the same handler. **This address does work**, with the account number in `?id=` or as `userID` in the body.

**A signed-in caller must be an administrator.** A bearer key is gated by the `users:write` scope alone -- nothing in the key path performs an administrator test -- plus the `api.users.update.enabled` switch, **which ships switched off**.

At least one of `fullName`, `isActive`, `isAdmin` or `isSiteAdmin` must be sent. **`isAdmin` is read only for a signed-in caller** and ignored for a bearer key -- so a key sending only `isAdmin` is refused for having sent nothing to change.

**A request that changes nothing writes nothing** and answers 200 with the stored values, on purpose, so re-sending a value cannot overwrite somebody else's concurrent change. Note the limit this leaves: a field that IS changing is read and then written two statements apart, without locking the row.

**`emailAddress` and any password field are silently ignored.** You cannot deactivate your own account through this endpoint.

post.summary: Register this device for push notifications
post.description:
Stores a browser's push details so the portal can notify this device.

**A signed-in person is required** -- this was not always so, and a request that is not signed in is now refused with 401 before anything else is read. A form token is required too.

**This endpoint does NOT use the portal's usual `{status, data, meta}` envelope.** It answers a flat object, and the replacement form token arrives as a top-level `csrf_token`, not as `meta.csrfToken`. Its answers carry none of the portal's usual security headers.

**Re-registering a device re-points it at whoever is signed in now**, because the stored row is keyed on the endpoint. A channel the portal does not recognise is dropped in silence rather than refused; if that leaves nothing, the default pair is used.

**Rate limited to 30 requests an hour per address, shared with `POST /api/push/unsubscribe`** -- the two endpoints count against one allowance. No `Retry-After` is sent.

Switches one device's push registration off. The row is kept and marked inactive rather than deleted.

**No sign-in is required**, deliberately: knowing the device's own push address is treated as proof enough, so a device whose person has gone can still switch itself off. A form token is still required.

**This endpoint does NOT use the portal's usual envelope**; the replacement form token arrives as a top-level `csrf_token`.

**It answers `ok: true` even when the address matched nothing**, and it is not scoped to an organisation -- a known address is switched off whichever organisation the request arrived at. Unlike subscribing, the address is not checked against the push services the portal recognises.

**Rate limited to 30 requests an hour per address, shared with `POST /api/push/subscribe`.** No `Retry-After` is sent.

post.summary: Record a scanned asset during a stocktake
post.description:
Records one scan against an open stocktake run -- the same action the stocktake screen performs, so a hand-held scanner can use it directly.

Needs the `assets:write` scope for a bearer key, or a signed-in administrator with a form token.

**A confidential asset is reported back without its name or number to a bearer key** -- `assetName` becomes `(confidential asset)` and `assetID` is left out altogether. `verifyStatus` is always returned and the scan is always recorded, so hiding the identity never hides that a scan happened.

**Every failure answers 404**: an unknown run, a run already closed and a code that is not recognised are deliberately indistinguishable. The message says which in words, but the status does not.

**For a bearer key the scan is recorded against no person**, because a key is not somebody.

code.description: The code that was scanned, as read from the label.

foundLocationID.description: Where the asset was actually found. A value that does not resolve is dropped rather than refused.

csrf_token.description: The form token, for a signed-in caller. May be sent in the `X-CSRF-TOKEN` header instead. Not used by a bearer key.

verifyStatus.description: What the scan established about the asset, for example that it was found where it was expected. Always present.

assetID.description: The asset that was scanned. **Left out entirely** when a bearer key scans a confidential asset.

assetName.description: The asset's name, or the fixed text `(confidential asset)` when a bearer key scans a confidential asset.

post.summary: Upload a picture or video for a noticeboard poster
post.description:
Takes one picture or video and stores it outside the web root, returning the address to show it at.

**Send it as `multipart/form-data`, and put the form token in the `X-CSRF-TOKEN` header** -- it CANNOT go in the body here, because the body is the file rather than JSON.

**The file's type is decided by inspecting its contents**, never from its name or the type the caller declares. Only PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, MP4 and WebM are accepted. The stored name is generated by the portal and the caller's filename is never used.

**The returned address is built for this organisation** and the picture is then served by a public address that needs no sign-in, because posters are shared by QR code.

The size limit is the installation's `noticeboard.upload.maxBytes`, falling back to 15 MB if that is not usable, so the cap can never be switched off. Note the web server's own upload limits apply first and produce a 400 of their own.

A signed-in caller must be an administrator of this organisation. A bearer key needs the `noticeboard:write` scope, and the organisation-administrator test does not apply to it: a key's authority is its scope.

get.summary: Search hymns and songs while building a service plan
get.description:
Searches this organisation's hymn book and song library, and an outside catalogue when one is configured, for the service-plan editor's type-ahead. Any signed-in person; an API key cannot reach this.

**Read `source` on each result to know where it came from** -- the three groups are returned one after another in a single list, local hymn book first.

**Nothing here is refused for being too long or too large.** `q` is shortened to 100 characters and `limit` is forced into the range 1 to 25, both silently. An empty `q` returns an empty list at once.

**It degrades quietly rather than failing.** A problem reading the song library leaves that group simply missing from an otherwise normal 200, and an outside catalogue that cannot be reached is skipped while `remoteAttempted` still reports true. So `remoteAttempted` tells you the outside search was switched on, NOT that it succeeded.

The organisation is always taken from the session; it can never be chosen by the caller.

parameters.description: What to search for. Shortened to 100 characters rather than refused. Empty returns an empty list.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many results to return per group. Forced into the range 1 to 25 rather than refused.

200.description: The results, or an empty list.

results.description: The matches, local hymn book first, then the song library, then the outside catalogue.

remoteAttempted.description: True when searching the outside catalogue is switched on. It does NOT mean that search succeeded -- a failure is skipped in silence.
